**0.11.0 is a breaking release.** It moves the storage and protocol format to format epoch 7. A 0.11 node refuses epoch-6 Raft WAL directories and object-storage prefixes at startup and refuses 0.10 peers, and a 0.10 node refuses 0.11 peers. The backup format stays 5, so `ursulactl restore` of 0.11 restores a 0.10 backup. There is no in-place upgrade, no rolling upgrade and no rollback.

- **If you cannot move your data yet, stay on 0.10.1.**
- **Deploy 0.11 fresh and move your data with a backup.** Install 0.11 on empty PVCs and never-used object-storage prefixes for the cold store and S3 snapshots, with the 0.10 cluster's `server.cluster_id` and `raft.group_count`. Stop client writes and every SQLite session, back up 0.10 with `ursulactl backup-create` and `backup-verify` of 0.10, stop the 0.10 nodes, copy their cold objects into the 0.11 cold root, skipping `URSULA_FORMAT_EPOCH` and `snapshots/`, and run `ursulactl restore` of 0.11, which checks the copy first. Every restored stream answers with a new `Stream-Incarnation`.
- **`helm upgrade` from 0.10 stops at the first pod**, which finds the 0.10 data on its volume and exits. Recover with `helm rollback`. Keep the peer lists of 0.10 and 0.11 nodes apart.
- **The gateway gives a request time for its size** ([#891](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/891)). `ursulagw` waits for a node's answer for `--response-header-timeout` plus the time the node needs to store or copy the request's bytes at 8 MiB per second: its body, or the parts a snapshot commit copies. A large append, create, snapshot or commit no longer gets `504` while the node still works on it. The VFS waits the same allowance beyond its own 15 s, which counts a commit's parts the same way, so it gives up after any gateway in front of the node. An object store slower than 8 MiB per second still needs a higher `--response-header-timeout` (`gateway.responseHeaderTimeoutSeconds`).
- **`ursula_stream::MAX_COLD_SNAPSHOT_BYTES` and its `ursula_runtime` re-export are removed.** Use `ursula_headers::MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES`, the same 1 GiB.

Every change is listed in the [0.11.0 release notes](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/release-notes#0110), and installing 0.11.0 is described in [Upgrading to 0.11](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/operations#upgrading-to-011).
